answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique smartcard PIN retry counter flips the bet — a card whose wrong-PIN counter never reset suspiciously — and the vine lands on the attacker instead. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the island compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the umber of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
